from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: Why do diseases spread?", ["Diseases spread through population interactions.", "Individuals occupy three distinct states.", "Susceptible, Infectious, and Recovered."])
        
        # Define nodes
        s_node = Circle(radius=0.4, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        s_label = Text("S", font_size=24)
        s_group = VGroup(s_node, s_label)
        
        i_node = Circle(radius=0.4, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        i_label = Text("I", font_size=24)
        i_group = VGroup(i_node, i_label)
        
        r_node = Circle(radius=0.4, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        r_label = Text("R", font_size=24)
        r_group = VGroup(r_node, r_label)
        
        self.place_at_grid(s_group, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(i_group, 'B4')
        self.place_at_grid(r_group, 'B6')
        
        transmission_arrow = Arrow(start=s_node.get_right(), end=i_node.get_left(), color=WHITE)
        
        self.add(s_group, i_group, r_group)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Initialize SIR model components on screen
        self.play(Create(transmission_arrow))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight S, I, R in colors
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            s_node.animate.set_color("#FFD700"),
            i_node.animate.set_color("#FF4500"),
            r_node.animate.set_color("#00CED1"),
            transmission_arrow.animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Emphasize state labels
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            s_label.animate.set_color("#FFD700"),
            i_label.animate.set_color("#FF4500"),
            r_label.animate.set_color("#00CED1")
        )
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Foundations: The Flow of Transitions", [
            "Arrows represent flows between states.",
            "Infection moves Susceptible to Infectious.",
            "Recovery moves Infectious to Recovered."
        ])

        self.lecture[1].set_color(RED)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Curves", [
            "The SIR graph shows disease dynamics.",
            "Infection peaks as Susceptible count drops.",
            "Flattening the curve reduces peak infection.",
            "Social distancing lowers the peak significantly.",
            "Geometry explains real-world policy impact."
        ])
        
        # Colors for lecture lines
        colors = [BLUE, GREEN, YELLOW, ORANGE, RED]
        
        # Setup graph elements
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 10, 1], y_range=[0, 1, 0.2], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "D6")
        
        s_curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.9 * np.exp(-0.5 * x), color=BLUE)
        i_curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * x * np.exp(-0.5 * x), color=RED)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(colors[0]), Create(axes))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(colors[1]), Create(s_curve), Create(i_curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Represent flattening by shrinking i_curve
        new_i_curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.25 * x * np.exp(-0.5 * x), color=RED)
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(colors[2]), Transform(i_curve, new_i_curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Pulse effect
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(colors[3]), i_curve.animate.set_stroke(width=6))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(colors[4]))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "R-naught is the reproduction number.",
            "It predicts secondary infections per person.",
            "R-naught over one means exponential growth."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Application: The R-Naught (R₀) Concept", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        r0_def = MathTex("R_0 = \\text{Reproduction Number}", color=YELLOW)
        curve_up = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.exp(x), x_range=[0, 1.5], color=RED)
        curve_down = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 1.0 * np.exp(-x), x_range=[0, 1.5], color=BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(r0_def, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(r0_def))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(curve_up, 'E2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(curve_down, 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(curve_up), Create(curve_down))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Indicate(curve_up))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Models simplify complex biological realities.", "Vaccines remove people from Susceptible.", "These tools ultimately save lives."]
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: From Models to Reality", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements for the right side
        sir_label = Text("SIR Model", font_size=24, color=BLUE)
        vaccine_label = Text("Vaccinated", font_size=24, color=GREEN)
        
        # Placeholder shapes for visualization
        sir_curve = ParametricFunction(lambda t: np.array([t, 0.5*np.sin(t*2), 0]), t_range=[0, 3], color=BLUE)
        vaccine_curve = ParametricFunction(lambda t: np.array([t, 0.2*np.sin(t*2), 0]), t_range=[0, 3], color=GREEN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(sir_label, 'A1')
        self.place_in_area(sir_curve, 'B1', 'C3')
        self.play(Write(sir_label), Create(sir_curve))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.place_at_grid(vaccine_label, 'A4')
        self.place_in_area(vaccine_curve, 'B4', 'C6')
        self.play(Write(vaccine_label), Create(vaccine_curve))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        final_message = Text("Predicting outcomes saves lives.", font_size=32, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(final_message, 'D1', 'F6')
        self.play(FadeIn(final_message))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Decoding Epidemics: The SIR Model Mechanics
outline.target_audience: University Students (Introductory Data Science or Biology)

sections.title: The Hook: Why do diseases spread?
sections.content: Introduce the concept of population dynamics using a simple visualization. Define the three key states: Susceptible (S), Infectious (I), and Recovered (R). Emphasize that every individual exists in one of these buckets at any given time.
sections.example: A digital simulation of a 'Zombie Outbreak' in a small school campus where healthy students (S) turn into zombies (I) upon contact, then become immune/cured (R).

sections.title: Mathematical Foundations: The Flow of Transitions
sections.content: Introduce the prerequisite concept of 'Rate of Change' (derivatives) through arrows. Explain the movement: S → I (infection rate) and I → R (recovery rate). Show how the 'S to I' transition depends on the density of both groups.
sections.example: An animation showing water flowing between three interconnected tanks: Tank S flows into Tank I, and Tank I flows into Tank R.

sections.title: Visualizing the Curves
sections.content: Display the classic SIR graph. Explain the 'Epidemic Peak': why I eventually declines (the exhaustion of S). Connect the geometry of the curves to real-world policy outcomes, such as 'flattening the curve'.
sections.example: A dynamic line graph that morphs in real-time as the instructor toggles the 'Infection Rate' variable, showing how social distancing lowers the peak of the I-curve.

sections.title: Application: The R-Naught (R₀) Concept
sections.content: Explain R₀ as the 'reproduction number'—how many secondary cases one person generates. Connect this back to the SIR equations: if R₀ > 1, the disease grows; if R₀ < 1, the disease dies out.
sections.example: A visual 'Tree of Infection' diagram showing one patient zero infecting three people, who each infect three more, illustrating exponential growth vs. controlled spread.

sections.title: Conclusion: From Models to Reality
sections.content: Summarize that models are simplifications. Briefly mention that reality adds complexity (births, deaths, vaccines). Reiterate that these tools allow scientists to predict outcomes and save lives.
sections.example: A final visual overlay comparing a basic SIR curve with a 'Vaccination Included' curve, showing how a portion of the population is removed from the S category immediately.
